draft.title: Reliable and valid assessment
card: a test that gives the same result each time it is repeated under the same conditions. A reliable test is consistent.
a test that measures what it is meant to measure. A sit-and-reach test is valid for hamstring and lower back flexibility, but not for aerobic power.
a result that is close to the true value. A heart rate monitor that reads 2 beats from the true rate is more accurate than one that reads 15 beats away.
A test can be reliable but not valid, because it can give the same wrong result every time. Using the same method, equipment and conditions each time helps make results reliable.
draft.remember: Reliable means consistent, valid means measuring the right thing, accurate means close to the true value.

a.q: Tom does a grip strength test three times in one session and gets 41 kg, 41 kg and 42 kg. Which word best describes the test?
opts: Reliable, because the results are very similar
Valid, because the results are very similar
Accurate, because the results are very similar
Reliable, because the results are all high
a.why: Results that agree when the test is repeated show the test is reliable. Similar results do not show that the test measures the right thing, so valid is wrong. They also do not show the results are close to the true value.
a.clue: Think about what repeating a test checks.

b.q: Priya's coach uses a 10 m walk to test the aerobic power of her netball team. Each player gets almost the same score every time. What is the best judgement of this test?
opts: Reliable but not valid for aerobic power
Valid but not reliable for aerobic power
Both reliable and valid for aerobic power
Neither reliable nor valid for aerobic power
b.why: The scores are the same each time, so the test is reliable. A short walk does not measure aerobic power, so it is not valid. The tempting answer is both, but consistent results do not prove a test measures the right thing.
b.clue: Does a short walk measure aerobic power?

a.best: Reliable, because the results are very similar

b.best: Reliable but not valid for aerobic power
